purpose: Add bounded cooperative intrachain collapse while preserving the linear model's high-contact behavior and Rg plateau. The cooperative attraction strengthens the collapse at low contact density but its marginal contribution dies off once q >> q_sat, so the marginal slope returns to b(T) instead of growing without bound as an unchecked negative m^2 term does.
description: This document is the CONTRACT for the third contact-potential family. It states the exact implemented equations, the parameters and their bounds, the limiting behavior, the multi-chain rule, the metadata every run must record, and the validation requirements. It supersedes the earlier design note for the implemented model: A(T) is temperature-independent (A0) and m_ref is fixed at 0. The optional temperature-dependent extension A(T) = h_A/T - s_A is listed under future_extensions and is NOT implemented.

implemented_in.registry_key_note: The MODEL_REGISTRY key is saturating_cooperative_contact; the potential_kind recorded in outputs is saturating_cooperative. There is exactly one registry key -- no alias.

variables.m: Raw nonbonded intrachain contact count for ONE chain (lattice count; the molecular-to-lattice contact offset is never applied inside the Hamiltonian).
variables.N: Number of beads in the chain (runtime chain length).
variables.m_ref: Reference contact count used to center q. Fixed at 0 in this implementation and recorded explicitly in every output.
variables.q: Intensive contact density q = (m - m_ref)/N = m/N, since m_ref = 0.
variables.T: Temperature in the same units as the fitted Tref/Tscale.

equations.effective_energy: H(C;T) = T * u  (temperature-dependent effective energy, NOT a temperature-independent microscopic energy)
equations.linear_part_evaluation: The linear part is evaluated as b(T)*m, NOT as N*(b(T)*(m/N)). The two agree in exact arithmetic, but the round trip through m/N and back through *N introduces floating-point drift; evaluating b(T)*m directly is what makes A0 = 0 reproduce the hs potential bit for bit.
equations.marginal_slope: du/dm = b(T) - A0 * d/dq[ q^2/(1 + (q/q_sat)^2) ], which tends to b(T) as q/q_sat -> infinity.

parameters.order_note: Parameter order is authoritative and identical in the fitter, the samplers and every output; params vectors are always written in this order.

h_b.meaning: enthalpic part of the linear contact bias, b(T) = h_b/T - s_b

s_b.meaning: entropic part of the linear contact bias, b(T) = h_b/T - s_b

A0.meaning: amplitude of the saturating cooperative attraction
A0.domain_reason: A0 is an attraction amplitude; a negative A0 would be a repulsion dressed up as one.
A0.nesting_role: A0 is the NESTED EXTRA TERM. At A0 = 0 the potential collapses exactly onto the linear hs model.

q_sat.meaning: contact density at which the cooperative attraction stops strengthening
q_sat.domain_reason: q_sat is a saturation scale; q_sat = 0 divides by zero and a negative value is meaningless.
q_sat.identifiability: q_sat enters the potential ONLY multiplied by A0. When A0 is not resolved away from zero, q_sat is NOT identified by the data and must be reported as weakly identified rather than interpreted as a physical saturation density.

parameters.chain_length_rule: N is required because q = m/N. The RUNTIME N is authoritative; the chain length the model was FIT at is recorded separately as provenance and a mismatch is a permitted, reported chain-length transfer.

limiting_behavior.A0_zero: u(m,T;N) = b(T)*m exactly, for every q_sat and every N. The model nests hs bit for bit: an A0 = 0 run reproduces the seeded hs trajectory, and q_sat has no effect on the potential at all.
limiting_behavior.m_zero: u(0,T;N) = 0 for every parameter set (q = 0 makes both terms vanish).
limiting_behavior.low_q: For q << q_sat the cooperative term expands as A0*q^2 * (1 - (q/q_sat)^2 + ...), so u ~ N*(b(T)*q - A0*q^2) + N*A0*q^4/q_sat^2: negative-quadratic cooperativity plus a positive-quartic stabilization. The residual against the pure quadratic form scales as q^4.
limiting_behavior.high_q: For q >> q_sat the cooperative correction C(q) = -N*A0*q^2/(1 + (q/q_sat)^2) approaches the finite plateau -P with P = N*A0*q_sat^2, so the potential returns to a straight line of slope b(T) offset downward by a bounded amount. With r = q/q_sat these are two DIFFERENT quantities and must not be confused: the fraction of the plateau MAGNITUDE already reached is |C(q)|/P = r^2/(1 + r^2), while the remaining signed distance ABOVE the plateau is C(q) - (-P) = P/(1 + r^2). The two are complementary and sum to P.
limiting_behavior.boundedness: The cooperative correction is bounded below by -N*A0*q_sat^2 for all m; it can never drive unbounded overcollapse.
limiting_behavior.extensivity: At fixed q, u/N is independent of N.
limiting_behavior.expected_effect: Sharper collapse than the linear model without the continued overcollapse caused by an unchecked negative m^2 term.

multichain_rule.equation: u(X,T) = lambda_intra * sum_alpha u(m_intra_alpha, T; N) + lambda_inter * b(T) * m_inter + kappa_bend * n_bend_total
multichain_rule.per_chain_requirement: Evaluate the saturating intrachain term SEPARATELY for every chain alpha using that chain's own cached m_intra_alpha and the runtime N.
multichain_rule.prohibited: Do NOT apply the nonlinear function to the total intrachain contacts sum_alpha m_intra_alpha, nor to m_intra + m_inter. Because u is nonlinear in m, that is a different potential and it manufactures artificial cross-chain coupling: two states with equal total intrachain contacts but different per-chain allocations genuinely have different potentials.
multichain_rule.interchain_term: Interchain contacts use the SAME fitted h_b and s_b through b(T) = h_b/T - s_b, but carry NO A0/q_sat correction. The single-chain fit does not identify an interchain cooperative term.
multichain_rule.lambda_controls: lambda_intra multiplies the COMPLETE per-chain intrachain potential; lambda_inter multiplies only the linear interchain term. They are independent multipliers.
multichain_rule.bending: kappa_bend * n_bend_total is a separate additive term, never folded into the contact model. Setting lambda_intra = lambda_inter = 0 does NOT disable bending.
multichain_rule.move_delta_rule: A proposed move's intrachain contribution is the exact difference of the full per-chain potential at the moved chain's old and new count, lambda_intra * (u(m_alpha + d_intra) - u(m_alpha)). It MUST NOT be approximated as b(T)*d_intra.
multichain_rule.swap_rule: log_accept = u(X_i,T_i) + u(X_j,T_j) - u(X_j,T_i) - u(X_i,T_j), evaluated through the same per-chain state-aware potential. The temperature-independent bending term cancels exactly.
multichain_rule.aggregate_helper_rule: Helpers that see only aggregate contact totals must REJECT this model explicitly; total intrachain contacts cannot determine the sum of the per-chain nonlinear potentials.

values.potential_definition: u(m,T;N) = N*[b(T)*q - A0*q^2/(1 + (q/q_sat)^2)],  b(T) = h_b/T - s_b,  q = m/N,  m_ref = 0,  A0 >= 0 and q_sat > 0 (both temperature-independent)
values.quadratic_normalization: empty string in NPZ / null in JSON -- this family has NO m^2/(2N) term and must not claim one

metadata_requirements.quadratic_coefficient: kappa(T), the coefficient of m^2/(2N), is identically 0 for this model. quadratic_coefficient_by_temperature is therefore all zeros and must NOT be read as evidence that the model is linear -- read potential_definition, A0 and q_sat instead.
metadata_requirements.named_parameters: A0 and q_sat are written as named scalars alongside the packed model_params vector, mirroring the h/s convention of the hs model.
metadata_requirements.npz_safety: All metadata values are strings, ints or floats -- no None and no object arrays -- so distributions NPZ files load with allow_pickle=False.
metadata_requirements.additivity: Every field above is ADDITIVE. No pre-existing field name, type or value is repurposed, so readers written against model API v1/v2 outputs keep working.

validation_requirements.parameter_domain: A0 >= 0, q_sat > 0, both finite, enforced when parameters are RESOLVED (validate_model_params / fit summary load), not lazily at the first potential evaluation. Out-of-domain parameters must raise rather than produce a silent NaN.
validation_requirements.exact_formula: u from the model API must equal a directly transcribed N*(b*q - A0*q^2/(1+(q/q_sat)^2)) to floating-point tolerance.
validation_requirements.nesting_regression: With A0 = 0 the potential must equal b(T)*m and a seeded sampler run must reproduce the corresponding hs run. Compare with exact equality (array_equal / ==), not a tolerance.
validation_requirements.legacy_preservation: Adding this model must leave every pre-existing model bit-for-bit unchanged: trajectories, observables, move counters, swap counts and potential values compared with ==.
validation_requirements.saturation: With P = N*A0*q_sat^2, r = q/q_sat and C(q) the cooperative correction, BOTH identities must hold numerically and must be tested as distinct quantities: the fraction of plateau magnitude reached, |C(q)|/P = r^2/(1+r^2), and the remaining signed distance above the plateau, C(q) - (-P) = P/(1+r^2), which sum to P. The numerical marginal slope du/dm must approach b(T) as r grows.
validation_requirements.extensivity: u/N at fixed q must be independent of N.
validation_requirements.per_chain_additivity: In the multi-chain sampler the intrachain potential must equal the sum over chains of u evaluated at each chain's own m_alpha.
validation_requirements.allocation_sensitivity: Two multi-chain states with equal TOTAL intrachain contacts but different per-chain allocations must have different potentials; a linear model must not be able to tell them apart.
validation_requirements.move_delta: The exact change in the full potential across an applied move must equal the per-chain full-potential difference plus the linear interchain and bending terms, and must differ from b(T)*delta_m whenever the moved chain's count changes.
validation_requirements.swap_consistency: The generalized swap must equal a manual four-potential calculation, and must be unchanged by any value of kappa_bend.
validation_requirements.determinism: Serial and multiprocessing runs must be bit-identical, including the per-chain contact cache carried across the process boundary.
validation_requirements.contract_parity: The fitter and the sampler must agree on API version, parameter names and order, potential_kind, potential_definition, potential_normalization, m_ref, requires_chain_length, numeric b(T), and the numeric FULL u(m,T;N) on a grid of temperatures and contact counts. Numeric checks must use NON-DEGENERATE probe parameters: at the registry x0 (A0 = 0) the potential is linear and the nonlinear code is never reached.
validation_requirements.insufficient_checks: b(T) alone cannot distinguish this model from hs or hs_m2_const at the same (h, s), and kappa(T) from raw_q_fn is identically zero here as well as for the linear models. Neither may be used as the only nonlinear contract check.
validation_requirements.identifiability_reporting: A0 is the nested extra term for uncertainty reporting: flag it when its bootstrap CI brackets zero or its fitted magnitude is negligible, and in that case report q_sat as WEAKLY IDENTIFIED rather than interpreting it as a saturation density.
validation_requirements.model_selection: Fit against both P(m|T) and P(Rg|T) and compare against the linear and contact-quadratic models on HELD-OUT temperatures. A nested model evaluated at its linear limit still fits; only an out-of-sample improvement supports the extra structure.

temperature_dependent_amplitude.equation: A(T) = h_A/T - s_A in place of the constant A0
temperature_dependent_amplitude.gate: Add only if cross-validation on held-out temperatures shows a clear improvement over constant A0.

interchain_cooperativity.description: A saturating cooperative term on interchain contacts
interchain_cooperativity.reason: A single-chain fit does not identify an interchain nonlinear term; adding one would require multi-chain data to constrain it.
